text:
sam: Hey — noticed a consistent 99th percentile tail spike in EU2 for dedicated pools this morning after the prefill run. CPU on the host is fine but NIC tx queue went to 100% and stayed there for ~30s.
anya: ugh. any packet drops or IGMP churn?
sam: drops small, but qlen backlog huge on eth0. tc shows long queuing by macvlan instances for tenant-42.
rohit: tenant-42 started a big batched-embed job around the same time? could be egress burst + affinity causing NIC hog.
kevin: can you paste the tc output? also which kernel irq settings on those nodes?
sam: sure, pasted below:
```
# tc -s qdisc show dev eth0
qdisc fq_codel 0: limit 10240pps
 Sent 1.2G bytes  packets 450k
backlog 22000p
qdisc pfifo_fast 1: pfifo limit 1000p
 Sent X bytes
```

sam: and /proc/interrupts had huge counts on eth0-Tx-0
anya: @rohit does this ring a bell with the new macvlan per-tenant plan? we spun up per-tenant veth/macvlan for isolation last week.
rohit: yep — the isolation helped flows but we didn't add per-tenant tx shaping. macvlan shares the same NIC queues, so a single tenant can congest tx.
kevin: is this only on dedicated pools or also on shared hosts?
sam: hit on dedicated pool hosts that also host <some shared infra> — scheduling ended up co-locating the prefilled instances with active tenants.
rohit: two quick mitigation ideas: 1) per-tenant egress policer at the host level (tc classful HTB qdiscs per macvlan) 2) prefer network-sparse placement when prefill runs.
anya: both have tradeoffs: policer adds CPU cost and a slight latency tax; placement reduces bin-packing efficiency and increases cloud spend.
kevin: what's the unit cost of keeping 10% more warm capacity for dedicated pools? we need numbers to balance against per-tenant shaping ops cost.
sam: rough calc: 10% warm in eu2 adds ~$1.8k/month for current fleet. Policing CPU + code path change estimated ~2 FTE-week to implement + 0.5k/mo infra.
rohit: we can prototype a lightweight egress-agent that uses XDP for per-macvlan rate limiting — lower CPU than tc and more predictable SLOs.
kevin: XDP work is non-trivial and risky to kernel interaction. ops prefers tc for quick rollout. ok, short-term: tc policer + placement tweak. medium-term: XDP egress-agent.
anya: agree. also add a canary that changes prefill scheduling to avoid co-locating with high-egress tenants for 24h. test results and rollback path.
sam: i'll open a small canary: prefill-avoid-label and shift allocation to lower-egress racks. canary scope: 3 racks eu2, 100 prefill jobs.
rohit: add telemetry: per-macvlan tx-queue depth, per-tenant packet drops, and per-node irq service time. we need good dashboards before rolling.
kevin: put cost comparison in the ticket (10% warm vs policing dev time vs XDP later). include expected latency delta for tail.
anya: also mention fallback: if tc doesn't help, we throttle tenant-42 job at scheduler layer (rate-limit API) and move to dedicated slice.
sam: noted. I'll create the ticket and a short runbook for oncall: 
- detect eth0 tx qlen > 10k for >10s
- check top 5 macvlan tx rates
- apply socalled temporary tc policing: `tc class add dev eth0 parent 1: classid 1:10 htb rate 300mbit`
- escalate to eng-infra if >3 occurrences/day

sre-bot: Incident detector: created alert infra.e2.egress_queue_backlog for node.* when qlen>10k for 10s (linked to ticket INFRA-3891).
rohit: cool. Sam, can you add tenant tagging in the alert so we can auto-attach the offending tenant id?
sam: yes — I'll update the alert rule to query per-macvlan labels.
kevin: timeline?
sam: will open ticket + small README today; aim to have tc policer canary + dashboards by EOD Fri.
anya: thanks — and add the cost summary so PMs can weigh in. :thumbsup:
kevin: one more ask: coordinate with sales ops to inform customers with dedicated pools about possible slight latency during prefill tuning. we don't want surprise SLA pings.
sam: yup will draft a short status blurb.
rohit: long term: let's revisit model routing — place heavy egress workloads into network-sliced subpools, not general dedicated pools. but that's a broader infra change.
kevin: noted. great plan.
